reader.requirement: At --std 85 the value FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED returns must denote the same instant as every compilation date and time the compiler provides in the listing of the source program (the page headings, the DATE-COMPILED paragraph's replacement, in every listing format) and in the generated object code, at whatever representation and precision each one uses; where the object code provides no compilation time, that half of the condition is not engaged.

edition-consulted.switches: the listing is on by default at --std 85 (std == 85), off by default at 2002/2014/2023; this decides whether the listing half of RV3 is engaged by default, not what instant the listing prints
the D8 edition window IntroducedIn <= DialectLevel (WHEN-COMPILED IntroducedIn 85 in IntrinsicCatalog), so the function binds at 85
the edition's year and standard name printed in the heading (ListingHeader Edition/EditionName); the instant beside them is the same CompilationInputs value at every edition

reader.edition-search: grep -i for WhenCompiled/WHEN-COMPILED/CompilationTime across src, then Edition|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior in src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Listing; the instant's capture (CompilationInputs.ReadCompilationTime), the 21-character form (CobolDate.Format21), the listing form (ListingTimestamp.Format) and the deterministic PE option in RoslynBackend.Compile consult no edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: only the default of the listing (on at --std 85, off at the later editions unless --listing is named); the shared-instant mechanism and both formats are the same code at every edition

reader.notes: One CompilationInputs instance per compilation (CompilerDriver.Compile) holds the one instant: whichever of the emitter's lazy WHEN-COMPILED stamp or the listing reads it first captures it, and the other reads the same value, so the heading, the DATE-COMPILED replacement and all three listing formats agree with the 21-character value; both formats truncate (seconds in the listing, hundredths in the value) from the same DateTimeOffset and offset. The object code is deterministic (PE TimeDateStamp is a hash), so it provides no other compilation time. The seed RoslynBackend.Compile is only the object-code half; the shared instant lives in CompilationInputs.ReadCompilationTime. A side observation, outside this rule: DISPLAY FUNCTION LENGTH (FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED) is refused at 85 with COBOL0900 (a numeric function outside an arithmetic expression).
